Marissa / team —

Quick update from infra: we've reproduced repeated p99 spikes tied to a small subset of requests with long prefix lengths (customer is sending long embeddings + long generation prompts in same request). On affected hosts we see KV cache churn + occasional GPU kernel stalls around the attention-backend path.

I attached a qps dump and a short host histogram. Immediate mitigations we can push in ~15m:
- Apply an aggressive prefix cache TTL to reduce KV cache misses (low-risk config change).
- Temporarily disable large-prefix batching for GlimmerPay routes to avoid oversized micro-batches.

Longer term we should consider a routing rule to shard very long requests to dedicated instances (but that's a roadmap item).

Attaching qps_dump.json and a trimmed log snippet.

Ben Carter
Principal Infra Engineer — Redwood

Folks —

We can do a fast fallback that should be safe and reversible:
1) Route GlimmerPay's GenAPI traffic to model-variant v1.3-small for the next 2 hours (drops peak token throughput but keeps latency stable).
2) Enable cache-priming for tokenization endpoints (prewarm common prefixes we see in traces).
3) Hold on any config that changes quantization thresholds — don't want regressions while customer is live.

Steps 1+2 are runnable from the control plane and I'll push a canary in 10m to 10% of traffic, monitor p95/p99 and errors, then ramp. Expected customer-visible improvement within 10-20 minutes after canary.

Also linking a short runbook extract for the control-plane rollback: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4821 (internal runbook).

Subject: Update: Investigation of intermittent latency spikes impacting Checkout

Alyssa —

Thanks again for the alert and trace bundle. Quick status: our engineering team has identified the likely cause as an interaction between long-prefix requests and cache churn on a subset of hosts. Actions underway:

- We've deployed a canary routing policy to divert 10% of your traffic to a stable, lower-throughput model variant (v1.3-small) to reduce tail latency.
- We applied a tighter prefix cache TTL and disabled large-prefix batching for your routes to limit KV churn.
- Monitoring is active; we'll provide a follow-up in 60 minutes with results and next steps.

Impact: you may see a slight reduction in peak throughput during the canary but we expect p99 to drop significantly and timeouts to stop.

If this message looks good, I'll send it and include the SRE contact (Ben) for technical follow-ups and our postmortem when available.

Regards,
